Question 1 of 20
Unit 1
What are the three components of the Leverage Equation that defines a 10x PMM?

✓ Correct!

The Leverage Equation captures how AI amplifies PMM work: saving time, maintaining quality, and enabling scale that was previously impossible.

✗ Not quite

The Leverage Equation is: Time saved × Quality maintained × Scale enabled. This is how AI amplifies PMM output.

Question 2 of 20
Unit 2
In the PMM Activity Audit, which cluster includes activities that become MORE valuable when routine work is automated?

✓ Correct!

Cluster 3 (Elevate) activities require human judgment, relationship-building, and strategic thinking—skills that become more valuable as routine work disappears.

✗ Not quite

Cluster 3 (Elevate) contains activities that become MORE valuable when the routine work around them is automated. This is where PMMs should focus their human energy.

Question 3 of 20
Unit 3
What's the fundamental shift in competitive intelligence that AI enables?

✓ Correct!

AI transforms CI from quarterly reports to always-on intelligence—continuous monitoring, real-time synthesis, and immediate alerting when competitors make moves.

✗ Not quite

The shift is from periodic research (quarterly competitive reviews) to continuous monitoring (always-on intelligence that catches competitor moves in real-time).

Question 4 of 20
Unit 4
In AI-assisted win-loss analysis, what's the primary value AI provides that humans can't match at scale?

✓ Correct!

AI can process hundreds of interview transcripts and identify patterns, themes, and insights that would take humans months to uncover manually.

✗ Not quite

AI's primary win-loss value is pattern extraction at scale—processing hundreds of transcripts to identify themes and insights that humans would miss or take months to find.

Question 5 of 20
Unit 5
What's the key difference between static battlecards and AI-enabled battlecards?

✓ Correct!

Dynamic battlecards update automatically when competitors make announcements and can surface deal-specific talking points based on the prospect's industry and situation.

✗ Not quite

AI-enabled battlecards are dynamic—they update automatically based on competitive changes and can provide context-specific guidance based on deal characteristics.

Question 6 of 20
Unit 6
In the Content Pyramid, which layer should PMMs INCREASE their personal time investment in?

✓ Correct!

As AI handles commodity content, PMMs should invest more in signature content—the thought leadership and original POV that only humans can create and that builds differentiated brand voice.

✗ Not quite

PMMs should increase time on signature content (thought leadership, original perspectives) while delegating commodity content to AI. Signature content is the differentiator.

Question 7 of 20
Unit 7
What does GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) optimize for that SEO doesn't?

✓ Correct!

GEO optimizes for AI citation—making your content structured, specific, and citable so that AI systems reference you when buyers ask questions about your category.

✗ Not quite

GEO focuses on being cited by AI systems (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot) when they answer buyer questions—a different optimization target than traditional search rankings.

Question 8 of 20
Unit 7
According to John Koblinsky's Evidence Assurance framework, what level of content gives AI "the receipts" to cite with confidence?

✓ Correct!

Auditable content is fully traceable to primary evidence—named customers, specific outcomes, verifiable claims. This is what AI can cite without looking stupid.

✗ Not quite

Auditable content has full traceability—"Accenture reduced cycle times 40%" vs. "industry-leading performance." Named customer, specific outcome, verifiable claim.

Question 9 of 20
Unit 8
What's the key shift in how sales enablement content should be structured for AI-assisted selling?

✓ Correct!

AI-assisted selling needs modular content tagged by use case, persona, and objection—so the AI can retrieve and assemble the right pieces for each specific deal context.

✗ Not quite

Content should be modular and tagged so AI can retrieve specific pieces and assemble them for each deal context—not monolithic documents that can't be parsed situationally.

Question 10 of 20
Unit 9
In AI-powered launch execution, what role does the PMM primarily play?

✓ Correct!

With AI handling content production and timeline automation, the PMM's value is in cross-functional orchestration, stakeholder alignment, and strategic decision-making.

✗ Not quite

When AI handles content production and timeline automation, the PMM's primary role becomes orchestration—aligning stakeholders, making strategic calls, and ensuring cross-functional coordination.

Question 11 of 20
Unit 10
What's the main advantage of AI-generated buyer personas over traditional persona development?

✓ Correct!

AI-generated personas can be created quickly and updated continuously as new customer data, market research, and win-loss insights become available—dynamic vs. static documents.

✗ Not quite

The advantage is speed and continuous updating—personas that evolve based on fresh customer data rather than becoming stale PDFs that no one references.

Question 12 of 20
Unit 11
Which of the four surviving skills is described as "the one AI is furthest from replicating"?

✓ Correct!

No agent can have the coffee conversation, read body language, or navigate the informal power structures that determine what actually gets done in organizations.

✗ Not quite

Organizational Intelligence—navigating stakeholders, reading body language, understanding hidden objections—is uniquely human and furthest from AI replication.

Question 13 of 20
Unit 11
In the T-Shaped PMM model, what does the vertical bar represent?

✓ Correct!

The vertical bar is your differentiator—deep expertise in strategic judgment, organizational intelligence, narrative craft, or customer empathy. This is what makes you irreplaceable.

✗ Not quite

The vertical bar represents deep expertise in one surviving skill—your differentiator that makes you irreplaceable, not just competent.

Question 14 of 20
Unit 11
What's the difference between customer knowledge and customer empathy?

✓ Correct!

Agents can provide data (usage patterns, NPS, tickets). Empathy is understanding feelings—frustration, anxiety, relief. That's why "Stop dreading Monday's forecast meeting" beats "Improve accuracy 34%."

✗ Not quite

Customer knowledge is data (usage, NPS, tickets). Customer empathy is understanding feelings—what it feels like to fight for budget, bet your reputation on a vendor, or finally solve a problem.

Question 15 of 20
Unit 6
What's the primary risk of using AI for content production without proper oversight?

✓ Correct!

AI presents everything in the same confident voice—whether built on evidence or hallucinated. Without human oversight, you risk publishing authoritative-sounding content that's wrong.

✗ Not quite

The risk is confident-sounding content that's factually wrong or off-brand. AI doesn't flag uncertainty—it sounds authoritative even when hallucinating.

Question 16 of 20
Unit 3
What are the three stages of an AI-powered CI pipeline?

✓ Correct!

Monitor (continuous tracking of competitor signals) → Synthesize (AI analysis and pattern detection) → Deliver (actionable intelligence to the right people at the right time).

✗ Not quite

The CI pipeline is: Monitor (track competitor signals) → Synthesize (AI analysis) → Deliver (actionable intelligence to stakeholders).

Question 17 of 20
Unit 7
Why does "Accenture reduced procurement cycle times by 40%" work better for GEO than "industry-leading performance"?

✓ Correct!

AI can cite specific, verifiable claims with confidence. "Industry-leading" gives AI nothing to work with—it's directional content with no evidence chain.

✗ Not quite

The difference is auditability—named customer, specific metric, verifiable outcome. AI can cite this confidently; "industry-leading" has no evidence to trace.

Question 18 of 20
Unit 1
What's the core insight of the "10x PMM" concept?

✓ Correct!

The 10x PMM isn't about working harder—it's about leverage. AI enables output impact that was previously impossible without dramatically increasing effort.

✗ Not quite

10x PMM means leverage, not effort. AI-augmented PMMs can achieve 10x the output impact because they've figured out what to outsource and what to keep.

Question 19 of 20
Unit 11
What are the three components of Narrative Craft?

✓ Correct!

Story Selection (right story for the moment), Specificity (concrete details, not abstractions), and Voice (authentic expression that makes your writing recognizably yours).

✗ Not quite

The three components are: Story Selection (matching stories to arguments), Specificity (concrete details), and Voice (authentic expression that's recognizably yours).

Question 20 of 20
Capstone
What makes someone a "10x PMM" in the agentic era?

✓ Correct!

The 10x PMM has the full T-shape: broad horizontal competence in agent-augmented work PLUS deep vertical expertise in one surviving skill. They've figured out what to outsource and what to keep.

✗ Not quite

The 10x PMM has both bars of the T: broad agent fluency (table stakes) + deep expertise in one surviving skill (differentiator). It's about leverage, not effort.
